Match the proverbs in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I (Proverbs)
List-II (Meanings)
 
(A) A nod is as good as
a wink to a blind horse
(I) Bad actions have worse consequences.
 
(B) First catch your hare (II) No point worrying about something before it
actually happens.
 
(C) Sow the wind and
reap the whirlwind
(III) A slight hint is enough to make someone
understand what you mean.
 
(D) Don’t meet trouble
halfway
(IV) No point in planning what you are going to
do with something until you actually have it.
 
 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
This question tests classical English proverbs: 'A nod is as good as a wink to a blind horse' signifies that a slight hint suffices (A-III); 'First catch your hare' advises against premature planning before acquiring what is necessary (B-IV); 'Sow the wind and reap the whirlwind' warns that minor destructive acts provoke catastrophic backlash (C-I); and 'Don't meet trouble halfway' cautions against borrowing trouble or unnecessary anticipatory anxiety (D-II). This gives (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.

questionText:
Rearrange the following phrases in the correct sequence to form a
meaningful sentence:
(A) despite its success and its scale, continues to
(B) proactively embrace transformational innovation opportunities
(C) a creative construction enterprise is one that
(D) pursue strategies, design systems and nourish cultures that
 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
The statement opens with the definition of the subject in (C) ('a creative construction enterprise is one that'). The concessive parenthetical phrase in (A) ('despite its success and its scale, continues to') leads into the compound verbal predicate in (D) ('pursue strategies, design systems and nourish cultures that'). The relative pronoun 'that' terminates in the action in (B) ('proactively embrace transformational innovation opportunities'). This establishes (C)-(A)-(D)-(B).
Hence, option (C) is correct.

The statement opens with the definition of the subject in (C) ('a creative construction enterprise is one that'). The concessive parenthetical phrase in (A) ('despite its success and its scale, continues to') leads into the compound verbal predicate in (D) ('pursue strategies, design systems and nourish cultures that'). The relative pronoun 'that' terminates in the action in (B) ('proactively embrace transformational innovation opportunities'). This establishes (C)-(A)-(D)-(B).
Hence, option (C) is correct.
